sentences.text: 1  MFA No. 4772/2017 CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS MFA COMING ON FOR HEARING, AFTER HAVING HEARD THE MATTER, RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT, THIS DAY,
RAMACHANDRA D.HUDDAR., J. PRONOUNCED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT The appellant/injured has preferred this appeal challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.177/2015 by the II Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chikkaballapura, vide judgment dated 5th May 2017 seeking enhancement of compensation on account of accidental injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident which occurred on 27.12.2014.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chikkaballapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties to this appeal are referred to as per their ranks before the MACT for the purpose of convenience.

3. It is the case of the petitioner/claimant that, on 27.12.2014 at about 4.00 p.m. when he was travelling as pillion rider on Bajaj Discover bike bearing Reg.No.KA-53-U- 818 with his friend Anand the rider near Shanimahatma Swamy temple Main Road cross of Bagepalli, the driver of bus bearing Regn.No.KA-40-4275 drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life dashed against the bike No.KA-53-U-818 from its hind side.
Due to the impact, both fell down and petitioner sustained injuries on his right hand, right leg, head and other parts of the body.
His friends shifted the petitioner to the Govt.Hospital, Bagepalli, provided first aid there.
Thereafter, for higher treatment, petitioner was shifted to HOSMAT Hospital, Bengaluru where he took further treatment.
4. A complaint was lodged in Bagepalli Police Station in Crime No. 269/2014.

Police on investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus for the offences punishable under 279,
337 and 338 of IPC.
The petitioner filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries suffered by him.
5. Before the MACT, respondent No.1 appeared and opposed the petition by filing the written statement.
Despite service of notice on respondent No.2-owner of the bus, he has not appeared before the MACT.

Therefore, he was placed ex- parte.
6.

In the written statement of respondent No.1, the whole case of the petitioner was denied with regard to the involvement of the bus, age, occupation, income of the petitioner, the medical expenses incurred by him and disability so alleged on account of injuries sustained.
It was contended that the compensation claimed was exorbitant.
It was prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. Based upon the rival pleadings of both the parties, the MACT framed relevant issues.

sentences.text: 8. To prove the case of the petitioner, he himself was examined as PW.1 and to prove the disability and treatment taken by him, examined Dr.Deepu N.K. of Hosmat Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to P26 and closed petitioners evidence.
Respondent No.1 has not led any evidence.
9. It is the case of the claimant that prior to accident, he was doing Real Estate business and agriculture and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month and he was the only earning member in the family.
Now his life has been paralysed due to the accident.

10. The learned MACT on hearing the arguments and on perusal of the records, held that the said accident had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver and awarded a compensation of Rs.2,16,000/- towards loss of future income.

In all, the MACT awarded a compensation of Rs.9,22,914/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization as per the table below:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No. Rs.
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000/-
 2. Medical Expenses 6,09,914/-
 3. Attendant charges, Nourishment 25,000/-
 of food and conveyance  4. Discomfort and loss of amenities 20,000/-
 5. Loss of earnings during laid-up 12,000/-
 period  6. Loss of future income 2,16,000/-
 TOTAL 9,22,914/-
11.
It further held that respondent No.2 being the Insured and respondent No.1 being the Insurer are liable to pay the compensation and respondent No.1 was directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Submissions of counsel for appellant 12.
The MACT has not taken into consideration the documents produced by the claimant in arriving at the just and reasonable compensation.
The award so passed is inadequate and grossly insufficient compared to the actual loss and damage caused to him.
The PW.2 doctor who issued disability certificate has assessed the disability at 31.38% considering the disability to the right upper limb.
But, the learned MACT has assessed the same at 20% to the whole body which is incorrect.
The medical records show the nature of injuries suffered/surgery undergone by the petitioner.
Therefore, prays to enhance the compensation.

sentences.text: Submission of counsel for Insurer 13.
The compensation awarded by the MACT is just one.
The MACT has correctly evaluated both oral and documentary evidence and has arrived at just and reasonable compensation.
That does not require interference of this Court.
Analysis 14.
The records of this case do reveal that, respondent No.1-Insurance Company has deposited the award amount before the MACT and MACT has released the same to the claimant.
Respondent No.1-Insurer has not preferred any appeal against fastening of liability to it.
Therefore, the finding with regard to liability of respondent No.1 to pay compensation has attained finality.
No finding is required to be given on the aspect of liability.
Now we have to delve upon the adequacy of the compensation awarded by the MACT.
15. PW.1 being the claimant has stated in his evidence about the injuries suffered by him in the said accident.
According to him, initially he was taken to Govt.Hospital, Bagepalli where he took first aid treatment.
Thereafter, on the advise of the Doctor, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment.
In the said Hospital, he underwent surgeries and was in-patient from 27.12.2014 to 12.01.2015 i.e. for almost 15 days.
The injures suffered by him were Right shoulder crushed at axillary fold externally (8 x 3 x 2 cm) in size., multiple exposed bleedings, bone exposed, multiple abrasions over arm and face.
Due to the said injuries, he has suffered permanent physical disability.
16. According to the claimant, he was an agriculturist as well as doing real Estate business and his monthly income was Rs.20,000/-, he was the sole earning member in the family.
Because of the accident, his family life has been crippled.
In support of his evidence, he has produced Ex.P4 wound certificate, Ex.P.6, Ex.P.10 to 13 medical receipts and bills.
He was cross-examined at length by the counsel for respondent no.1 but, nothing worth was elicited to impeach his evidence.
17. PW.2 Dr.Deepu N.K. was examined as the doctor who treated the claimant.

PW2 deposed that,
on medical examination of the petitioner, he noticed the following medical findings :
1. A severe crush injury of rt shoulder and arm extending 8 x 3 x 2 cm. from axillary crease with skin avulsion.
2. Muscles and bone exposed with bleeding from wound.
3. Range of motion of shoulder absent.
4. Multiple abrasions over forearm present.
5. Patient condition was unstable, was shifted to icu.
6. X-rays showed fracture clavicle Sri Prabhakara Reddy vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81197855/

sentences.text: Doppler showed thrembosis and injury to proximal axillary artery with no flow distally.
18. In the said hospital, certain medical procedures like wound debridement and axillary artery repair with vein graft+ deltoid and pectoralis major myorraphy+ and etc., were done.

When he examined the petitioner on 10.3.2017, he noticed restricted shoulder movements, wrist stiff and loss of movement, inability to hold anything in hand, cannot do any work, inability to ride vehicle,
inability to wear clothes by himself and complete loss of sensation of little and ring fingers.

He also noticed the following physical impairments:
1. 10 x7 cm over shoulder and 15 x 7 cm over rt arm afted insensate area over rt upper limb.
2. Restricted shoulder and wrist movements.
3. No grip strength in rt hand 4. Loss of sensation over rt little and ring finger.
19. According to the said doctor's evidence, claimant required future surgery which may require Rs.1,40,000/-.
Based upon the said clinical findings, he assessed the permanent partial disability for the right upper limb at 94.16% and to the whole body 31.38%.
He speaks about Ex.P26 the disability certificate issued by him and with regard to the disability of the claimant.
There were no grounds to disbelieve his evidence.
Therefore Tribunal should have considered permanent physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner atleast 31%.

20. On perusal of the medical records stated above, they do suggest that, as per contents of Ex.P4 being the wound certificate issued at the earliest point of time, the claimant was diagnosed with injuries "crush injury (right shoulder) with - 10 - axillary artery laceration and first clavical fracture right".
Both the injuries were grievous in nature.

To show that he had spent medical expenses, at the time of treatment, he had produced the prescriptions, bills at Ex.P6, P10 to 13 (Medical bills), Ex.P14 prescription, Ex.P16 - Medical bills and Ex.P15 discharge summary and reports.

The discharge summary shows that from 27.12.2014 to 12.01.2015, petitioner took the treatment as an in-patient at HOSMAT Hospital, the history was shown as petitioner has suffered accidental injuries.
The Tribunal, after evaluation of the said medical prescriptions and bills including in-patient cash bills, provisional bills and had arrived at Rs.6,09,914/-.
The said compensation awarded towards medical expenses is based upon the bills and requires no interference.
21. The Tribunal has assessed the loss of future income to the extent of Rs.2,16,000/- by assessing the total monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.1,200/- (Rs.6,000 x 20%) per month.

sentences.text: that petitioner is an agriculturist and also doing Real Estate Business and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, no document was produced in support of such contention.
In support of his agriculture income, he had produced RTC extract at Ex.P18 to 24.
In col. no.9 and 12 petitioner's name is - 11 - appearing and name of one P.Ashwath Reddy and other is appearing.
Even at col.no.12(9) of the RTC extracts, in some extracts it is shown as `no crop'.
To show that, he was really cultivating the said agricultural land, no evidence is placed on record.
Therefore, his contention that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from agriculture etc was not acceptable.
Therefore, his income has to be notionally assessed.

The accident was of the year 2014, considering age, occupation of the petitioner,
cost of living and prevailing wage rates during the said period, it would be just to consider his monthly income at Rs.8,500/- per month.
22. The whole body disability is assessed to the extent of 31%.
Thus, 31% of Rs.8,500/- comes to Rs.2,635/-.
It is to be calculated annually which comes to Rs.31,620/- (2635 x 12).
Claimant was aged 38 years at the time of accident as per the medical records.
As per Sarla Verma and Ors v.Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr1 case, the proper multiplier that is applicable is `15'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors v.Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus the loss of future income due to disability comes to Rs.4,74,300/-(Rs.31620 x 15).
23.

While assessing the compensation towards disability, it must not be lost sight of that loss of bodily 2009 (6) SCC 121 - 12 - integrity gives right to damages even if there is no damage at all to the earning capacity or even to enjoyment of life.

Because damages in such cases are awarded commensurate with the accident,
gravity and duration of the injury.

The test in case of bodily injury are to be as to whether the breaking of the physical integrity is of a temporary nature or permanent nature and what would be the impact and to what extent the physical incapability or temporary or permanent would be reflected in the earning capacity of the injured.
Therefore, loss of income due to disability is arrived at Rs.4,74,300/- keeping in mind the aforesaid concept.

24. Further, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs. Rs.25,000/- towards Attendant Charges,
Nourishment, food and conveyance, which is on lower side.
It requires to be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Further, in view of fractures sustained by the claimant, he must have been idled at least for a period of three months.
This possibility cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, loss of income during laid up period comes to Rs.25,500/- i.e., (Rs.8,500X3).
25.
As per the evidence of the doctor, the petitioner had suffered disability to the extent 31.38% to the whole body.

sentences.text:
In view of the treatment taken by the petitioner in a well- equipped HOSMAT Hospital, by this time,
the injuries must have been healed.
However, with all frustrations, inconvenience and disability, the petitioner has to survive.
The petitioner has to receive proper and just compensation for the injuries suffered by him.
It is well settled that compensation for personal injuries is higher as compared to fatal cases, since in the former case, it is to be utilised by the victim of the accident and
in the latter,
by the legal heirs.
It is true that compensation cannot bring back the victim to the stage he enjoyed before the accident, but, it would provide him some solace and security for future.

So also,
Rs.20,000/- awarded towards loss of amenities was on the lower side.

Hence, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
26.
As regards the compensation awarded under the head `Pain and Suffering' at Rs.40,000/-, we feel the same is on the lower side.
Having regard to the injuries sustained and the surgeries undergone by the petitioner, it is just and proper to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/-.
There is no acceptable evidence with regard to the future medical expenses except the say of PW.2.
Petitioner has not produced any records to show that he has underwent a subsequent surgery.
Therefore, we decline to grant any compensation under that head.
. Thus, the compensation to be awarded to the claimant is as per the below table:

6 . Loss of future income 4,74,300/-
 TOTAL 12,59,714/-
